Lab 03 — what to do, step by step (animated)

Step 1

Set up: Python, the lab folder, the evidence hashes

≈ 15 min
Animated drawing (self-made, schematic) — loops automatically
  1. Install Python 3 from python.org/downloads — 3.15.0 (released October 9, 2026) or 3.14.8. On Windows tick Add python.exe to PATH. The scripts use only the standard library: nothing else to install.
  2. Install an editor (VS Code or Notepad++) and a spreadsheet (LibreOffice Calc or Excel) to open the CSV (Comma-Separated Values) files.
  3. Download class15_files.zip (Class 15 module → Download all files) and lab3_evidence.zip (Léa). Check both with VirusTotal (Legal Notice, Annex C). You also need the Class 14 files (logon_failures.py, traffic_summary.py, security_export.csv, auth.log, packets.csv).
  4. Create Lab03_<StudentNumber>_<LastName>/ with 1_detect/, 2_sort/, 3_evidence/, report/; unzip the evidence into 3_evidence/ and verify the hashes — every line must say OK. Never edit an evidence file.
Commands / files for this step
python3 --version
mkdir 1_detect 2_sort 3_evidence report
cd 3_evidence && sha256sum -c hashes.sha256
# Windows PowerShell:  py --version   and   Get-FileHash * -Algorithm SHA256
The terminal looks different on Windows (PowerShell), macOS and Linux; the commands above are the same. If python.org shows a newer version than 3.15.0 when you read this, take it — the lab works with any Python 3.12 or later.
Step 2

Part A — Detect: run the three scripts and name every flag

≈ 45 min · 20 points
Animated drawing (self-made, schematic) — loops automatically
  1. Copy the three scripts and their input files into 1_detect/, then run them one after the other. Each one prints its flags and writes a CSV file next to the inputs.
  2. Expected: 2 ALERT lines from logon_failures.py, 2 flags from traffic_summary.py (port-scan pattern, no-reply SYN), 3 flagged hours from baseline_deviation.py.
  3. Write report/A_detections.md: one row per flag — source · rule · what was flagged · family (point / contextual / collective) · why that family — and the Topic 4 data source (event log, network traffic, system activity).
Commands / files for this step
cd 1_detect
python3 logon_failures.py
python3 traffic_summary.py
python3 baseline_deviation.py
A count inside a time window is a collective anomaly; one value far outside the band is a point anomaly; an ordinary value at an idle hour is a contextual anomaly (Class 15, lesson 5.1.3).
Step 3

Part B — Sort: run the triage script and read the queue

≈ 45 min · 20 points
Animated drawing (self-made, schematic) — loops automatically
  1. In 2_sort/ run alert_triage.py; it reads the twelve weekend alerts, the asset inventory, the allow-list and the maintenance calendar and writes triage_queue.csv: 4 × P1, 3 × P2, 1 × P3, 1 × P4, 3 benign.
  2. Write report/B_triage.md: the queue; one line per alert in your own words (impact = max(rule severity, asset criticality) + 1 if a privileged account; confidence = 3 ± the factors); any position you move by hand and the lesson 5.2.5 rule you apply; the outcome category of A-04, A-10 and A-11 and what it implies for Topic 6.
Commands / files for this step
cd ../2_sort
python3 alert_triage.py
# open triage_queue.csv in LibreOffice Calc / Excel to read and sort it
The spreadsheet view in the animation is schematic. In Calc, open the CSV with the comma separator; keep the column order so your marker can compare with the reference queue.
Step 4

Part C — Diagnose: timeline first, conclusion last (two P1 items)

≈ 2 h · 30 points
Animated drawing (self-made, schematic) — loops automatically
  1. Pick two of the four P1 items: the WS-10-44 story (A-02 with A-03 and A-08), A-05 (administrator failures from the VPN pool), A-06 (SSH guessing on srv-web01) or A-12 (srv-web01 silent).
  2. Open the evidence files named after the asset (ws-10-44_*, srv-ad01_* + vpn_*, srv-web01_*, mon-250_*) and build the timeline table: time · file · record quoted verbatim · interpretation. Sort by time before you reason.
  3. Test the benign explanations first (maintenance_calendar.csv, allowlist.csv, vpn_logbook.txt, the scheduled-task list), find a second independent source, then conclude: incident / benign / monitoring failure, the MITRE ATT&CK technique if there is an attacker, your confidence, what stays open.
  4. Answer the four Class 14 questions in report/C_diagnosis.md: who held 10.8.0.9; did any SSH logon on srv-web01 succeed; which process on WS-10-44 scanned and was the designer present; why srv-web01 went silent at 11:20.
Commands / files for this step
# useful one-liners (Linux/macOS; PowerShell: Select-String)
grep -n "Accepted" 3_evidence/srv-web01_auth_2026-10-10.log
grep -n "4740\|4625" 3_evidence/srv-ad01_security_2026-10-10.csv
grep -n "No space left" 3_evidence/mon-250_syslog_2026-10-09_10.log
The animation shows the A-05 timeline as an example of form, not as the answer to copy: your conclusion must quote the records you used. "No evidence of X" is not the same as "X did not happen".
Step 5

Part D — Report: one page for the owner, a technical annex for the contractor

≈ 45 min · 15 points
Animated drawing (self-made, schematic) — loops automatically
  1. Section 1, owner page: plain language, no abbreviations — what happened, what it could cost the firm (confidentiality, integrity, availability), what was done, what decision she must take.
  2. Section 2, technical annex: the timeline, the evidence references (file + row/line), the recommended containment → eradication → recovery → lessons learned, in priority order, following CCCS ITSAP.40.003 and NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3.
Commands / files for this step
report/D_report.md
# 1. For the owner (one page)
# 2. Technical annex (timeline · evidence · containment · eradication · recovery · lessons learned)
Write the owner page last, when you know what matters; write it as if the reader will decide something in the next ten minutes.
Step 6

Part E — Optimise: three changes and one tool, each justified

≈ 30 min · 10 points
Animated drawing (self-made, schematic) — loops automatically
  1. One baseline update (6.1), one tuning change that removes a benign alert without creating a false negative (6.4), one coverage improvement (6.3), one tool recommendation (6.5) taken from the alternatives table of the lab sheet.
  2. For each: what you change, why, which alert it affects, and why it does not hide a real incident. Write report/E_optimisation.md.
Commands / files for this step
report/E_optimisation.md
# 6.1 baseline · 6.4 tuning · 6.3 coverage · 6.5 tool
Free and open-source candidates for 6.5 (official sites): Wazuh, Security Onion, Graylog Open, Suricata, Zeek, Timesketch, DFIR-IRIS. Version numbers change every few months — cite the one you see on the official page the day you write.
Step 7

Zip the folder and submit it in Omnivox Léa

≈ 10 min · before Monday October 19, 2026, 23:59 EDT
Animated drawing (self-made, schematic) — loops automatically
  1. Zip the whole folder as Lab03_<StudentNumber>_<LastName>.zip: Markdown files, CSV outputs, the unchanged evidence — no installers, no virtual machines.
  2. Omnivox → Léa → 420-1C1-DW → Assignments / DropBox → Lab 03 → upload the zip → keep the confirmation (screenshot or e-mail). Léa records the upload time.
  3. Deadline Monday, October 19, 2026, 23:59 EDT. Late: −10 % per day; nothing accepted after 7 days. The last upload before the deadline is the one marked.
Commands / files for this step
# Windows (PowerShell):  Compress-Archive -Path .\Lab03_2630180_Tremblay -DestinationPath .\Lab03_2630180_Tremblay.zip
# macOS / Linux:        zip -r Lab03_2630180_Tremblay.zip Lab03_2630180_Tremblay
Léa's real screens are different from this drawing and change with Omnivox updates; the menu may be called "Assignments", "Travaux" or "DropBox". The steps are always the same: open the course, open the assignment, upload the zip, keep the confirmation.

Before you upload — checklist

  • 1_detect/: 3 scripts, their inputs, 3 output CSV files
  • report/A_detections.md: 7 flags, family + data source each
  • 2_sort/: alert_triage.py + triage_queue.csv
  • report/B_triage.md: queue, reasons, hand changes with rule, outcome categories
  • 3_evidence/: 13 files, hashes OK, nothing edited
  • report/C_diagnosis.md: two P1 items, verbatim timelines, conclusions, four Class 14 questions answered
  • report/D_report.md: owner page + technical annex
  • report/E_optimisation.md: 6.1 · 6.4 · 6.3 · 6.5, justified
  • zip named Lab03_<StudentNumber>_<LastName>.zip
  • uploaded in Léa before October 19, 23:59 EDT; confirmation kept
